subject: Proposal: regional fallback lanes and buffer sizing for Altair Labs conversion
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: regional fallback lanes and buffer sizing for Altair Labs conversion

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Altair’s conversion timeline looks like a classic multi-region ramp: initial US + EU launch in Q4, APAC pilot in Q1, and then steady growth after month three. To keep the app snappy we recommend a small dedicated pool per geography plus cross-region fallback lanes.

Attached is an initial worksheet (altair_mrp_requirements.xlsx) and a short capacity proposal PDF that outlines three scenarios: conservative, expected, and surge. Quick summary of our ask from you: can you confirm expected peak concurrent requests/sec and any hard SLOs (p99 latency target) for inference? That’ll let us finalize sizing.

High-level proposal (first pass):
- US pool: 6 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (steady), burst to 12 during sales campaigns
- EU pool: 4 dedicated GPUs, burst to 8 with regional caching enabled
- APAC pilot: 2 dedicated GPUs for Singapore pilot, scale to 6 after validation
- Cross-region fallback: policy to failover APAC->EU->US for non-sensitive workloads; sensitive traffic stays pinned to region or private deployment

Next steps: Irene will follow up with a micro-sizing spreadsheet and latency/cost tradeoffs. If these numbers look in the right ballpark, we’ll draft an SOW and attach a tranche-based activation schedule.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@altairlabs.ai>

Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@altairlabs.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: regional fallback lanes and buffer sizing for Altair Labs conversion

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for this—PDF and worksheet received. Quick answers from our side:
- Peak expected qps (inference requests): 450 qps peak for US during campaign peaks, baseline ~120 qps
- EU peak: 180 qps; APAC baseline for pilot: 40 qps, target after rollout ~160 qps
- p99 latency target: <= 250ms for customer-facing responses (hard), internal batch tasks can be 500ms
- Data residency: EU production traffic must remain within EU for PII workflows; APAC pilot initially can use Singapore region but sensitive workflows will require local processing later

We’re open to a tranche activation (pilot -> regional ramp -> steady-state). Can you provide a cost delta between burst-to-capacity vs reserve-commit pricing in the proposal? Also can you call out expected unit cost/token for the three model families we discussed (small, base, and cross-attention quantized)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround—Tom and I will review the details and revert by EOD.

Cheers,
Sarah Jones
Head of ML Platforms, Altair Labs
sarah.jones@altairlabs.ai
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: regional fallback lanes and buffer sizing for Altair Labs conversion

Vanessa / Rishi —

I pulled the APAC/EU/US micro-sizing and a quick cost sketch based on Altair’s qps numbers. Key assumptions: 8k token/session average, model mix: 60% base (B), 30% small (S), 10% cross-attn quantized (Q). We recommend keeping a 20% buffer above expected peak to cover bursty usage and planned campaigns.

Proposed dedicated pools (with 20% buffer):
- US steady: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) — handles ~540 qps peak with autoscale headroom to 14 for campaign bursts
- EU steady: 5 GPUs — handles ~220 qps peak, EU-only routing for sensitive traffic
- APAC pilot: 3 GPUs (Singapore) — handles ~48 qps baseline and spikes to 200 qps after full rollout; plan to add two more GPUs at T+60 days if utilization >70%

Fallback lanes and policy notes:
- Fallback routing: APAC->EU allowed for non-PII; EU->US not allowed for EU-sensitive traffic
- Cache layer: prefix caching will reduce token cost for repeat prompts by ~18-25% depending on workload
- Quantization: Q model yields ~2.3x token throughput improvement but expect slight quality delta — recommend A/B eval during pilot

Estimated cost tradeoffs (high level):
- Reserve commit (12-month) reduces unit GPU-hour by ~28% vs on-demand burst; burst-to-capacity ideal for campaigns, but reserve is cheaper for steady high-utilization periods
- We’ll include exact per-token numbers in the formal proposal PDF (attached draft SOW will include pricing appendix)

I’ve attached SOW draft and the micro-sizing sheet. Let me know if you want me to reduce buffer to 10% for a conservative price.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments:

Subject: Re: Proposal: regional fallback lanes and buffer sizing for Altair Labs conversion

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the quick details — Irene’s attached micro-sizing reflects those numbers and includes the 20% buffer she mentioned. A few clarifications based on your asks below:

- Cost delta between reserve vs burst: for the proposed steady pools (US 8, EU 5, APAC 3), reserve-commit 12mo is ~28% cheaper vs on-demand. If you expect steady utilization above 50% in any region we strongly recommend a reserve tranche for that region.
- Per-token estimates: small= $0.0006/token, base= $0.0014/token, quantized cross-attn= $0.0009/token (these are estimates tied to model family + quantization profile; final numbers in pricing appendix)
- SLO handling: we will keep EU-sensitive flows pinned; fallback lanes are configured at the request-routing layer and can be overridden per API key / customer ID.

If this direction looks good, I’ll push a formal SOW and tranche schedule to HubSpot and DocuSign. Proposed milestone cadence:
1) Pilot activation (APAC) — sign SOW v1, 2-week pilot provisioning
2) EU+US steady activation — tranche 1 reserve commitment for US and EU, 30-day ramp
3) Campaign burst window — provision additional burst capacity and reconcile billing post-campaign

Can you confirm by EOD Friday whether you want us to price the conservative (10% buffer) or standard (20% buffer) option so we can lock numbers?

Onward —
Vanessa
